page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz on x86_64 architecture with the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, using a burstable CPU allocation model. It features 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). System cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 480 MB of L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions. The instance relies on network-attached storage with no local NVMe SSDs included, features zero GPUs, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, c8i-flex.xlarge demonstrates strong single-threaded execution capabilities. It ranks in the top quartile for single-threaded gzip compression (34.08 GB/sec), single-threaded bzip3 decompression (13.94 GB/sec), Geekbench single-core score (2110.0), and Geekbench text processing (2789.0). Conversely, multi-core throughput displays constraints under sustained compute loads due to the 2 physical core count and burstable allocation model, placing multi-threaded stress-ng (4301.36) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (27.63 GB/sec) in the lower quartile. Memory throughput yields middle-tier results for large data blocks (40.9 GB/sec read, 28.5 GB/sec write). Operational benchmarks reflect mid-range performance, recording 7.68 million Redis SET operations per second, 7.95 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and 34.85 tokens/sec for medium-model (7B) LLM prompt processing.

From a resource design perspective, c8i-flex.xlarge provides cost-effective single-core execution for non-continuous workload profiles. The combination of DDR5 memory, Intel AMX acceleration, and high clock speeds supports microservices, text processing, static web serving, and periodic batch processing jobs. However, workloads requiring sustained multi-core throughput, large memory footprints, or low-latency high-throughput networking will experience bottlenecks under this resource profile.
